newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt to decide on economic meet closer to time.
newsitem.headline: Egypt to decide on economic meet closer to time.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak said on Tuesday his country had not yet decided whether it would attend a controversial Arab-Israeli economic conference due to be held in Qatar in November.

Mubarak, touring the site of a large irrigation scheme near the southern province of Aswan, also told reporters he hoped the Palestinians and Israel would make progress towards kick-starting their stalled peace talks within the next 10 days.
Qatar is due to host the fourth Middle East/North Africa (MENA) economic economic conference since landmark Middle East peace negotiations began in 1991.
The Gulf state has said it is committed to holding the gathering but it has come under pressure from some Arab countries which are angry at Israel's policies about peace.
Peace talks between Israel and the Palestinians collapsed in March after the Jewish state began building a new settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince Abdullah said in remarks published on Monday the kingdom would not attend the Doha gathering and that Riyadh had advised Qatar to cancel it.

Asked if Prince Abdullah had advised Egypt to boycott the conference, Mubarak said: "He didn't give me such advice. Each country makes its own decision in the proper time. I cannot tell you that I am going. It depends on the situation just before the conference."
Egypt had threatened to delay last year's conference, which it hosted, over Israel's failure to implement self-rule deals with the Palestine Liberation Organisation.
